Sanitization is idempotent, so downstream paths call it without knowing whether an upstream path already did (`checkpoint.sanitizeForAgentType` is the store's belt-and-braces call). The agent's own transcript is never modified. Coupling to respect: `SessionState.CheckpointTranscriptSize` is a growth baseline compared against the shadow transcript blob size in `sessionHasNewContent`, so it must be measured in the same sanitized (pre-externalization) coordinate — that is `CondenseResult.TranscriptSizeBaseline`; using the raw size makes the comparison false forever and the session silently stops condensing.
 - **Redaction cost and the two mechanisms that contain it.** Redaction dominates the Stop hook on a large session: it is ~99.7% of the metadata-walk blob write (git object writing is milliseconds), and ~82% of that is the betterleaks regex ruleset. Two things keep it bounded, and both rest on redaction being **per-line and stateless** (`redact.redactJSONLLines`) — a rule that looked at neighbouring lines would silently break both:
   - `jsonlContentImpl` shards the line pass into ~1MiB byte-balanced groups across goroutines. Output is byte-identical to the sequential pass. Sharding is gated on an explicit `concurrencySafe` argument describing the **redactor**, not on which entry point was called: `String` is pure and opts in (including `batch.go`'s OPF-disabled fast path), while the OPF collector closures accumulate into a shared map/slice and pass `concurrencyUnsafeRedactor`. Shards are balanced by bytes rather than line count because transcripts mix short lines with occasional multi-MB tool results.
-  - The checkpoint metadata walk reuses the previous checkpoint's redacted blob as a prefix and redacts only appended lines (`checkpoint/redact_cache.go`), turning a per-Stop cost of O(whole transcript) into O(appended). The stored prefix must always end immediately after a `\n`, which is what makes plain byte concatenation reproduce the full result; content with a partial trailing line is therefore never cached. Reuse requires the prefix bytes to still hash the same and `redactionFingerprint()` (CLI version + commit + `redact.ConfigFingerprint()`) to match, so a rewritten transcript, changed custom rules, or a CLI upgrade all fall back to a full redaction. Bump `configFingerprintVersion` in `redact/fingerprint.go` whenever the regex layers change behaviour, or stale output can be reused. 24	// Transcripts are append-only JSONL, but every checkpoint used to re-redact them
25	// from byte zero: a 70MB Codex rollout cost ~67s per Stop hook, and a session
26	// with N checkpoints re-redacted O(N^2) bytes overall. Redaction is ~99.7% of
27	// that write path (git object writing is milliseconds), and it is by far the
28	// dominant cost of a Stop hook on a large session.
29	//
30	// So keep the redacted output for the prefix already processed and redact only
31	// what was appended. Correctness rests on two properties:
32	//
33	//   - Redaction is per-line and stateless (see redact.redactJSONLLines), so
34	//     redacting a prefix and a suffix separately and concatenating them yields
35	//     exactly what redacting the whole file would. redact's own tests pin this
36	//     as redact(A+B) == redact(A)+redact(B) for newline-terminated A.
37	//   - A cached prefix always ends immediately after a "\n". Because of that the
38	//     redacted prefix also ends with "\n", and plain byte concatenation
39	//     reproduces the full result with no boundary fixups.
40	//
41	// The prefix is only reused when the source bytes it covered still hash the
42	// same and the redaction rules have not changed. Anything else -- a rewritten
43	// transcript, a compaction, changed custom rules, a CLI upgrade -- falls back to
44	// redacting everything.
45	//
46	// Scope: all three whole-transcript paths reuse prefixes -- the shadow-branch
47	// metadata write, post-commit condensation
48	// (strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go), and the Stop finalize rewrite
49	// (strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go). The latter two arrive here through
50	// RedactTranscriptIncremental. Single-JSON-value transcripts (OpenCode export)
51	// still get only the sharding in redact.JSONLContent, since they have no line
52	// structure to split on.
53	//
54	// The three paths do NOT all redact the same bytes, which is why entries are
55	// namespaced by TranscriptScope: the shadow write stores a sanitized transcript,
56	// while condensation and finalize store a sanitized *and* image-externalized one
57	// (see prepareTranscriptForStorage). Sharing one key across those would be safe --
58	// the prefix hash check rejects a mismatch -- but it would miss on every
59	// checkpoint, so each scope gets its own namespace and its own hit rate.

61	const (
62		// RedactCacheDirName sits in the git common dir, NOT under .entire/, because
63		// anything inside the worktree metadata directory would be walked into the
64		// checkpoint tree and committed.
65		//
66		// Exported so `entire clean` can reclaim it: every entry is derived data that
67		// is rebuilt on the next checkpoint, so the whole directory is safe to delete
68		// at any time.

72		// worth its bookkeeping; a small file redacts in milliseconds.

76	// redactPrefixEntry is the persisted record of one file's already-redacted
77	// prefix. Written atomically; a missing, unreadable, or stale entry simply means
78	// a full redaction.
79	type redactPrefixEntry struct {
80		// Fingerprint identifies the redaction rules that produced RedactedBlob.
81		Fingerprint string `json:"fingerprint"`
82		// SourceBytes is the length of the source prefix covered, always ending
83		// immediately after a newline.
84		SourceBytes int `json:"source_bytes"`

89		RedactedBlob string `json:"redacted_blob"`

93	// the git common dir. A nil *redactCache disables incremental reuse, which is

96		dir string

99	// newRedactCache returns a cache rooted at gitCommonDir, or nil when the

101	func newRedactCache(gitCommonDir string) *redactCache {

118	func repoRedactCache(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository) *redactCache {
119		dir, err := resolveGitCommonDir(ctx, repo)

128	// ruleset and the pipeline itself, neither of which is introspectable: an
129	// upgrade invalidates every cached prefix and costs one full redaction.
130	func redactionFingerprint() string {
131		return versioninfo.Version + ":" + versioninfo.Commit + ":" + redact.ConfigFingerprint()
132	}

134	func (c *redactCache) path(treePath string) string {
135		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(treePath))

139	func (c *redactCache) load(treePath string) *redactPrefixEntry {
140		data, err := os.ReadFile(c.path(treePath))
141		if err != nil {
142			return nil
143		}

145		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &entry); err != nil {

147		}

150		}

180	type redactResult struct {
181		// Redacted is the content to store. Nil means the caller must redact the
182		// whole content itself.
183		Redacted []byte
184		// SourceHash is the digest of the whole source, computed as a side effect of
185		// prefix validation so the caller never hashes the content a second time.

192	// incrementalRedactionCandidate reports whether a stored file is worth prefix
193	// caching: a large, append-only, line-delimited session transcript.
194	//
195	// Both checks below are load-bearing for different reasons, so neither is
196	// redundant:
197	//
198	//   - The filename establishes append-only. Only full.jsonl is appended to;
199	//     transcript.jsonl (the compact transcript) is regenerated in full each
200	//     checkpoint and agent.ChunkFileName yields "full.jsonl.001" for oversized
201	//     transcripts, so neither should qualify.
202	//   - redact.IsLineDelimited establishes that splicing is sound. The filename
203	//     alone is not a safe proxy: OpenCode writes a single JSON object
204	//     ({"info":...,"messages":[...]}) to this very path, and redacting a fragment
205	//     of a single JSON value drops out of the field-aware pass into raw entropy
206	//     detection over partial JSON.
207	func incrementalRedactionCandidate(content []byte, treePath string) bool {
208		return len(content) >= redactCacheMinBytes &&

213	// transcriptRedactor redacts a whole byte range. The same function redacts the
214	// appended suffix and, on a cache miss, the whole content -- passing one redactor
215	// for both is what makes it impossible to splice a prefix produced by one
216	// pipeline onto a suffix produced by another.
217	type transcriptRedactor func(ctx context.Context, content []byte) ([]byte, error)
218	
219	// redactIncrementally redacts content, reusing a previously redacted prefix when
220	// one is available and still valid.
221	func redactIncrementally(
222		ctx context.Context,
223		repo *git.Repository,
224		cache *redactCache,
225		content []byte,
226		treePath string,
227		redactor transcriptRedactor,
228	) (redactResult, error) {
229		if cache == nil || !incrementalRedactionCandidate(content, treePath) {
230			return redactResult{}, nil
231		}
232	
233		// Only a file ending on a line boundary can be cached, because the reuse
234		// contract requires the stored prefix to end just after a "\n".
235		if content[len(content)-1] != '\n' {
236			return redactResult{}, nil
237		}
238	
239		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "redaction")
240	
241		entry := cache.load(treePath)
242		if entry == nil || entry.Fingerprint != redactionFingerprint() || entry.SourceBytes > len(content) {
243			return redactResult{SourceHash: hashBytes(content), StorePrefix: true}, nil
244		}
245	
246		// Hash the prefix and the remainder in one pass: Sum snapshots the digest
247		// without resetting it, so validating the prefix also yields the whole-content
248		// hash the caller stores, instead of a second pass over ~70MB.
249		digest := sha256.New()
250		digest.Write(content[:entry.SourceBytes])
251		prefixHash := hex.EncodeToString(digest.Sum(nil))
252		digest.Write(content[entry.SourceBytes:])
253		fullHash := hex.EncodeToString(digest.Sum(nil))
254	
255		// The prefix must still be byte-identical; a rewritten or compacted
256		// transcript invalidates it.
257		if prefixHash != entry.SourceHash {
258			logging.Debug(logCtx, "redaction prefix changed, redacting in full",
259				slog.String("path", treePath), slog.Int("prefix_bytes", entry.SourceBytes))
260			return redactResult{SourceHash: fullHash, StorePrefix: true}, nil
261		}
262	
263		prefix, readErr := readBlobBytes(repo, plumbing.NewHash(entry.RedactedBlob))
264		if readErr != nil {
265			logging.Debug(logCtx, "cached redacted prefix unreadable, redacting in full",
266				slog.String("path", treePath), slog.String("error", readErr.Error()))
267			return redactResult{SourceHash: fullHash, StorePrefix: true}, nil
268		}
269		// A prefix that does not end on a newline would corrupt the join, so refuse
270		// it rather than emit spliced output.
271		if len(prefix) > 0 && prefix[len(prefix)-1] != '\n' {
272			logging.Debug(logCtx, "cached redacted prefix does not end at a line boundary, redacting in full",
273				slog.String("path", treePath))
274			return redactResult{SourceHash: fullHash, StorePrefix: true}, nil
275		}
276	
277		if entry.SourceBytes == len(content) {
278			// Nothing appended since the last checkpoint: the stored entry already
279			// describes exactly this content, so there is nothing to re-record.
280			return redactResult{Redacted: prefix}, nil
281		}
282	
283		suffix := content[entry.SourceBytes:]
284		// A degraded scanner must not be spliced onto the reused prefix: fail the
285		// write instead of persisting an under-scanned suffix.
286		redactedSuffix, err := redactor(ctx, suffix)
287		if err != nil {
288			return redactResult{}, err
289		}
290		out := make([]byte, 0, len(prefix)+len(redactedSuffix))
291		out = append(out, prefix...)
292		out = append(out, redactedSuffix...)
293	
294		logging.Debug(logCtx, "redacted transcript incrementally",
295			slog.String("path", treePath),
296			slog.Int("reused_bytes", entry.SourceBytes),
297			slog.Int("redacted_bytes", len(suffix)))
298	
299		return redactResult{Redacted: out, SourceHash: fullHash, StorePrefix: true}, nil
300	}

302	func hashBytes(b []byte) string {
303		sum := sha256.Sum256(b)
304		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
305	}

307	// readBlobBytes loads a blob's full contents.
308	func readBlobBytes(repo *git.Repository, hash plumbing.Hash) ([]byte, error) {
309		blob, err := repo.BlobObject(hash)
310		if err != nil {
311			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read blob %s: %w", hash, err)
312		}
313		reader, err := blob.Reader()
314		if err != nil {
315			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open blob %s: %w", hash, err)
316		}
317		defer func() { _ = reader.Close() }()
318	
319		// blob.Size is known, so read into an exact buffer: io.ReadAll grows by
320		// doubling and allocates roughly 2.3x the payload for a large transcript.
321		out := make([]byte, blob.Size)
322		if _, err := io.ReadFull(reader, out); err != nil {
323			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read blob %s: %w", hash, err)
324		}
325		return out, nil
326	}

328	// TranscriptScope namespaces prefix-cache entries by the preprocessing a
329	// transcript went through before reaching redaction. Two scopes never share an
330	// entry, because their byte streams differ (see the file header).
331	type TranscriptScope string
332	
333	const (
334		// ShadowScope is the shadow-branch metadata write: sanitized, not
335		// image-externalized.
336		ShadowScope TranscriptScope = "shadow"
337		// CommittedScope is post-commit condensation and the Stop finalize rewrite:
338		// sanitized and image-externalized. Both store the same bytes for the same
339		// session, so they share a namespace and warm each other's prefix.
340		CommittedScope TranscriptScope = "committed"
341	)
342	
343	// transcriptCacheKey is the cache key for one session's transcript within a
344	// scope. It ends in paths.TranscriptFileName because
345	// incrementalRedactionCandidate gates on that basename, and it carries the
346	// session ID so concurrent sessions in one worktree never share an entry.
347	func transcriptCacheKey(scope TranscriptScope, sessionID string) string {
348		return string(scope) + "/" + sessionID + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileName
349	}
350	
351	// RedactTranscriptIncremental redacts a whole session transcript, reusing the
352	// prefix redacted for the previous checkpoint when it is still valid and
353	// recording this result for the next one. Output is byte-identical to redacting
354	// content in one pass; see the file header for why splicing is sound.
355	//
356	// This is the entry point for the paths that hold a transcript in memory rather
357	// than walking a file (condensation and the Stop finalize rewrite). Those paths
358	// re-redacted the full transcript on every checkpoint, which is what made a Stop
359	// hook on a 65MB Codex rollout exceed Codex's 30s hook timeout outright rather
360	// than merely run slow.
361	//
362	// redactor supplies the pipeline, and is used both for the appended suffix and
363	// for the whole content on a miss, so the two can never diverge. Everything here
364	// is best-effort: an unresolvable git dir, an unreadable cached blob, or a
365	// rewritten prefix all fall back to redacting everything, and only a redactor
366	// error propagates.
367	func RedactTranscriptIncremental(
368		ctx context.Context,
369		repo *git.Repository,
370		scope TranscriptScope,
371		sessionID string,
372		content []byte,
373		redactor func(ctx context.Context, content []byte) (redact.RedactedBytes, error),
374	) (redact.RedactedBytes, error) {
375		full := func(ctx context.Context, b []byte) ([]byte, error) {
376			out, err := redactor(ctx, b)
377			if err != nil {
378				return nil, err
379			}
380			return out.Bytes(), nil
381		}
382	
383		// A missing session ID would collide every session onto one key, so decline
384		// caching rather than risk cross-session reuse. The hash check would reject
385		// the mismatch anyway; this just avoids the pointless churn.
386		if repo == nil || sessionID == "" {
387			return redactor(ctx, content)
388		}
389	
390		treePath := transcriptCacheKey(scope, sessionID)
391		cache := repoRedactCache(ctx, repo)
392	
393		result, err := redactIncrementally(ctx, repo, cache, content, treePath, full)
394		if err != nil {
395			return redact.RedactedBytes{}, err
396		}
397		if result.Redacted == nil {
398			redacted, redErr := redactor(ctx, content)
399			if redErr != nil {
400				return redact.RedactedBytes{}, redErr
401			}
402			result.Redacted = redacted.Bytes()
403		}
404	
405		if result.StorePrefix {
406			// The blob is written for the cache's benefit; the checkpoint store writes
407			// the same bytes again, and git dedups it to the same object.
408			if blob, blobErr := CreateBlobFromContent(repo, result.Redacted); blobErr == nil {
409				cache.storePrefix(ctx, treePath, result.SourceHash, len(content), blob)
410			}
411		}
412	
413		return redact.AlreadyRedacted(result.Redacted), nil
414	}
